text:
Sunset's just past, and if you were out for it, you saw it clean, clear skies, 86 dropping toward a comfortable-feeling low around 67 tonight with the humidity still low. Any lingering shower or rumble wraps up by 8, and the rest of the night stays calm, light south winds under 10 knots on the lake and waves a foot or less if anyone's still out there.

Tomorrow's the one to plan around. NWS has Tuesday at a high near 86 with a 60% chance of showers and storms arriving mid-afternoon and lingering into the evening, and the models back that up, the European's notably wetter than the American guidance, so I'd lean into the higher chance. This is also the front edge of a slow-moving system the forecasters expect to bring widespread rain Tuesday through Thursday, with some risk of localized flooding, so it's not a one-and-done. On the lake, south winds 10 to 15 knots and waves building to 1-3 feet Tuesday afternoon. Get your morning in early; by early afternoon I'd have boats off the water and plans indoors.
